lines.en: Whoa, whoa, whoa, whoa! Watch out for this guy.
Dwight Schrute in the building.
This is Ryan, the new temp.
What's up?
Nice to meet you. Introduce yourself. Be polite.
Uh, Dwight Schrute, assistant regional manager.
Assistant to the regional manager.
So, uh, Dwight, tell him about the, uh, the kung fu
and the, uh, car and everything.
Uh, yeah, I got a, uh, '78 280Z.
I bought it for $1,200. Fixed it up. It's now worth $3,000.
That is his profit.
Yeah. Uh, new engine, suspension.
I got a respray. I got some photos.
Uh, damn it!
Okay. Hold on, hold on.
Judge is in session. What is the problem here?
He put my stuff in Jell-O again.
That's real professional. Thanks.
This is the third time, and it wasn't funny the first two times I've hurt you.
All right, all right. What is that?
It's my staple.
No, no, no, no! Do not take it out.
You have to eat it out of there, because there are starving people in the world,
and which I hate, and it is a waste of that kind of food.
Okay, you know what? You can be a witness. Can you reprimand him, please?
How do you know it was me?
It's always you. Are you going to discipline him or not?
Ooh, discipline. Kinky.
All right. Here's the deal, you guys.
The thing about a practical joke is that you have to know when to start as well as when to stop.
Yeah.
And, yeah. And, Jim, now is the time to stop putting Dwight's personal effects into Jell-O.
Okay. Dwight, I'm sorry, because I have always been your biggest flan.
Oh, nice! That's the way it is around here. It just kind of goes around and around and around.
You, uh, you should have put him in custody.
Oh, hey! Yes! New guy! And he scores!
Okay, that's great. I guess what I'm most concerned with is damage to company property. That's all.
Pudding. Pudding. I'm trying to think of another dessert to do.
